subtopics.title: Why Assets Lose Value in the Books

questions.question: The matching principle demands depreciation because:
options: The asset earns income over many years, so its cost must be spread as an expense over those same years
Assets must always be shown at market value
The owner prefers smaller profits
SARS requires all assets to be written off in year one

questions.question: The figure that never moves after purchase day is:
options: The carrying value
Cost price — anchored by the historical cost principle
Accumulated depreciation
The year's depreciation charge

questions.question: Accumulated Depreciation on Vehicles is best described as:
options: An income account
A liability owed to the garage
A negative asset account beside Vehicles, gathering all the value written off since purchase
The bakkie's resale price

questions.question: The annual depreciation double entry is:
options: Debit Vehicles; credit Depreciation
Debit Accumulated Depreciation; credit Bank
Debit Bank; credit Vehicles
Debit Depreciation; credit Accumulated Depreciation on Vehicles — cost stays anchored

questions.question: The bakkie (R150 000 at 20% per annum on cost) depreciates each year by:
options: R30 000 — the same slice every year, because the base never changes

questions.question: At the end of year two on straight-line, the three figures read:
options: Cost 150 000; accumulated 30 000; carrying value 120 000
Cost 120 000; accumulated 60 000; carrying value 60 000
Cost 150 000; accumulated 60 000; carrying value 90 000
Cost 90 000; accumulated 60 000; carrying value 30 000

questions.question: At 20% on cost, the whole cost is consumed in:
options: Ten years
Five years — though the books often leave R1 standing for an asset still in use
Four years
It is never consumed

questions.question: Straight-line is the honest choice for:
options: Assets that work hardest when new
Assets bought mid-year only
Assets with no cost price
Assets that serve roughly evenly across their life — office equipment, fittings, furniture

subtopics.title: Diminishing Balance, and Additions During the Year

questions.question: Year two on diminishing balance (R150 000 at 20%) charges:
options: R30 000 — 20% of cost
R24 000 — 20% of the R120 000 carrying value

questions.question: Under diminishing balance, the carrying value:
options: Reaches zero in exactly five years
Falls by the same amount every year
Slides toward zero without ever arriving — the method never fully consumes the asset
Rises in years of low use

questions.question: Diminishing balance suits vehicles and machines because:
options: They give their best, hardest years first — big years carry big charges, tired years small ones
Their cost price changes yearly
They never wear out
The rate is easier to remember

questions.question: The computer (R24 000, straight-line 15%, bought 1 November, year end 28 February) is charged in its first year:
options: R3 600 — the full year
R1 200 — R3 600 times four months over twelve

subtopics.title: The Asset Register and Exam Technique

questions.question: The asset register relates to the ledger the way:
options: The budget relates to the cash book
A list of debtors relates to its control account — detail whose totals must agree with the summary
The journal relates to the trial balance
An invoice relates to a receipt

questions.question: An asset on the register that cannot be produced on inspection signals:
options: Nothing — registers are often out of date
That depreciation was overcharged
Possible theft or loss — the register has a question that must be answered
That the asset was fully written off

questions.question: The words 'on carrying value' in a question tell you to:
options: Use the diminishing balance method — the shrinking base
Use straight-line
Ignore accumulated depreciation
Charge a full year regardless of purchase date

questions.question: The three figures must stay labelled in your working because:
options: The register has three columns
Only carrying value is ever asked
Labels earn no marks but look neat
A question asks for one of depreciation, accumulated or carrying value — and answering with another scores nothing

subtopics.title: The Bakkie That Quietly Gets Cheaper

questions.question: The year-old phone that still works but sells for two-thirds of its price shows that:
options: Value falls with age and newer models, even when nothing breaks
Phones are poor investments
Depreciation only applies to damaged goods
The books should ignore working assets

questions.question: Keeping the bakkie at R150 000 in the books for five years would be:
options: Required by the historical cost principle
A polite lie — the books must record the wearing
Correct if the bakkie still runs
Prudent accounting

questions.question: 'Receipt, wear, worth' stands for:
options: Three depreciation methods
The purchase documents in the register
Cost price, accumulated depreciation, and carrying value
Invoice, delivery note, statement

subtopics.title: Two Ways to Slice the Loss

questions.question: The 'same slice every year' way cuts:
options: Twenty percent of whatever is left
Twenty percent of the original R150 000 — R30 000 level slices until the loaf is gone
A different percentage each year
Slices only in profitable years

questions.question: The 'fifth of what's left' way gives slices of:
options: 30 000, then 24 000, then 19 200 — each smaller than the last

questions.question: Diminishing balance is honest for the bakkie because:
options: Its biggest, hardest working years come first, so they carry the biggest slices
Bakkies never lose value
It writes the asset off faster in later years
The rate rises as the bakkie ages

questions.question: The trap in year two is beaten by:
options: Always using the original cost
Averaging the two methods
Saying the base out loud before you cut — original loaf for straight-line, what's left for diminishing balance
Doubling the first year's charge

subtopics.title: Every Asset Gets Its Own Page

questions.question: 'Totals upstairs, faces downstairs' means:
options: The ledger holds one summary line while the register holds each asset's own page — and they must agree
Assets are stored on two floors
The register is kept in the basement
Only the ledger matters at year end

questions.question: The November computer's page starts with a R1 200 first-year charge because:
options: Computers depreciate slowly
It served only four of the twelve months — charged for the months it actually worked
The rate was reduced to 5%
Mid-year assets skip their first year

questions.question: A register page that lists a computer nobody can produce has just:
options: Proved the ledger wrong
Completed the audit
Shown the depreciation rate was too low
Caught a possible theft — or started a very serious conversation

questions.question: For the replace-or-repair decision, the register supplies:
options: The asset's age, remaining value and repair history — the facts the decision needs
The bank balance
Next year's sales forecast
The supplier's newest catalogue
